propositions: The primary completion-verify agent step is dispatched with no tool_step_limit boundary, so a runaway tool-call cycle exhausts the entire 240-request budget and dies with no verdict, leaving --force-close as the only exit.
Repetition detection exists (max_consecutive_repeat) but is blind to cycles of length ≥2, so it under-reports pathological runs while scoring healthy ones higher (inverted metric).

The windowed distinct-ratio discriminator (window 24 calls, threshold ≤0.50, order-insensitive) reliably separates looping runs from healthy breadth across all measured cases, firing on pathological runs at ratios 0.042-0.290 and never on healthy runs with ratio ≥0.833.

The shipped forced-landing mechanism (tools withdrawn via run_step boundary) breaks on Bedrock/Anthropic when history contains tool_use blocks and toolConfig is omitted, causing protocol-level 400 errors instead of graceful landing.

Synthetic tool-result steering (WrapperToolset returning a steering message instead of executing repeated calls) lands the agent naturally without protocol violations, allowing the verdict to flow through the normal structured-output path.

A typed RunawayToolLoopError branch in interpret_failure must precede the generic LLMUnavailableError fallback, so runaway loops are never misreported as provider outages, and CompletionAgentStep.run can route them to bounded recovery.
